tools.description: List all webhook sources in the organization. A source is an ingest endpoint that receives incoming webhooks from a provider like GitHub or Stripe and records them as events — it forwards nothing on its own until hookbase_create_route connects it to a destination. Returns summary fields including eventCount and routeCount; use hookbase_get_source for one source's full configuration.
tools.name: hookbase_list_sources

tools.description: Get full configuration for a single source, including its allowed HTTP methods, rate limit, and signature-verification settings. The signing secret itself is never returned here — only hasSigningSecret and signingSecretLast4; use hookbase_reveal_source_secret to read the full value. awaitingSigningSecret=true means no secret is stored and only the vendor can issue one (e.g. Stripe or Shopify when the create omitted it, or Asana/Notion, which issue it only after the ingest URL is registered), so events are accepted but not verified until it is set with hookbase_update_source signing_secret (or, for Notion, adopted via hookbase_adopt_source_pending_verification). verifiesWithoutSecret=true means the provider publishes a key Hookbase already has (wise, aws-sns), so events are verified with no secret.
tools.name: hookbase_get_source

tools.description: Create a new webhook source. Sources receive incoming webhooks and can be connected to destinations via routes. Before creating one for a named vendor, call hookbase_get_provider to find the right provider value and its secretSource: if it is "provider" or "public_key", ask the user for the vendor-issued secret/key and pass it as signing_secret (for public keys and format-checked vendor keys such as Standard Webhooks/svix the API rejects the create without it; for the rest the source is created with no secret and awaitingSigningSecret=true, so events are not verified until it is set); if it is "operator", omit signing_secret and give the user the returned signingSecret to paste into the vendor — it is shown only here (hookbase_reveal_source_secret can read it later). The response also carries ingestUrl (the URL to register with the vendor), verifyToken for WhatsApp/Meta, and awaitingSigningSecret=true when no secret was stored for a vendor-issued provider (including Asana and Notion, which issue it only after the URL is registered).

allowed_methods.description: HTTP methods this source's ingest endpoint accepts. Omit or pass [] to accept any method. GET/HEAD/DELETE carry no body, so their query string becomes the event payload.

provider.description: Webhook provider, which selects the signature scheme used to verify incoming requests. Common values: "github", "stripe", "shopify", "slack", "gitlab", "twilio", "paddle", "sendgrid", "whatsapp", "standard-webhooks", "custom". Not sure of the exact value? Call hookbase_list_providers (search by vendor name) and use the entry's hookbaseProvider — the catalog id can differ — then hookbase_get_provider to learn whether the user must paste a secret (secretSource). Omit it for a source that should accept unsigned requests. Use "standard-webhooks" (alias "svix") for any sender built on Standard Webhooks / Svix; "clerk", "resend", "render", "etsy" and "stytch" are accepted as aliases for it. Use "custom" (alias "generic") for a sender that signs the raw body with HMAC-SHA256 in its own header. An unknown value is rejected by the API with a 400.

reject_invalid_signatures.description: Whether to reject webhooks with invalid signatures

signing_secret.description: Signing secret (or public key) used to verify this source's webhooks. Whether to send it depends on the provider's secretSource (see hookbase_get_provider): "provider" — the vendor issues it, so ask the user to paste it (required for Standard Webhooks/svix/clerk/resend, airtable, gitlab-signing-token, and supabase-auth-hooks, and format-checked); "public_key" — paste the vendor's public key (required); "operator" — omit it and Hookbase generates one, returned once as signingSecret for the user to paste into the vendor; "built_in" (wise, wise-sandbox, aws-sns) — never send one (400); "none" — optional, only for a custom HMAC secret. Asana and Notion issue their secret only after the URL is registered: omit it on create.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier, lowercase letters, digits and dashes (e.g., "github-webhooks")

transient_mode.description: Enable transient mode - payloads never stored at rest (HIPAA/GDPR compliance). Disables replay and payload viewing.

verify_token.description: WhatsApp/Meta only (the API returns 400 for any other provider): the "Verify token" Meta checks when the URL is registered. Omit it and Hookbase generates one, returned as verifyToken.

tools.name: hookbase_create_source

tools.description: Update an existing source's configuration — name, provider, signing secret, verify token, signature enforcement, rate limit, transient mode, or allowed methods. Only the fields you provide are changed; omitted fields keep their current value. Switching to a provider whose secret the vendor issues requires signing_secret in the same update. Turning on reject_invalid_signatures immediately starts rejecting webhooks that fail verification; turning on transient_mode stops new payloads from being stored at rest but does not retroactively delete payloads already stored. To have Hookbase generate a fresh secret use hookbase_rotate_source_secret instead. Returns only a confirmation — call hookbase_get_source (or hookbase_get_source_verify_token) to read the result.

allowed_methods.description: HTTP methods this source's ingest endpoint accepts. Omit or pass [] to accept any method. GET/HEAD/DELETE carry no body, so their query string becomes the event payload. Pass [] to revert to accepting any method.

provider.description: Change the source's provider (null clears it). Webhook provider, which selects the signature scheme used to verify incoming requests. Common values: "github", "stripe", "shopify", "slack", "gitlab", "twilio", "paddle", "sendgrid", "whatsapp", "standard-webhooks", "custom". Not sure of the exact value? Call hookbase_list_providers (search by vendor name) and use the entry's hookbaseProvider — the catalog id can differ — then hookbase_get_provider to learn whether the user must paste a secret (secretSource). Omit it for a source that should accept unsigned requests. Use "standard-webhooks" (alias "svix") for any sender built on Standard Webhooks / Svix; "clerk", "resend", "render", "etsy" and "stytch" are accepted as aliases for it. Use "custom" (alias "generic") for a sender that signs the raw body with HMAC-SHA256 in its own header. An unknown value is rejected by the API with a 400.

signing_secret.description: Set the signing secret (e.g. one the user copied from the vendor, or Asana's secret once it has been issued); null removes it. Takes effect immediately — the old secret stops verifying. Signing secret (or public key) used to verify this source's webhooks. Whether to send it depends on the provider's secretSource (see hookbase_get_provider): "provider" — the vendor issues it, so ask the user to paste it (required for Standard Webhooks/svix/clerk/resend, airtable, gitlab-signing-token, and supabase-auth-hooks, and format-checked); "public_key" — paste the vendor's public key (required); "operator" — omit it and Hookbase generates one, returned once as signingSecret for the user to paste into the vendor; "built_in" (wise, wise-sandbox, aws-sns) — never send one (400); "none" — optional, only for a custom HMAC secret. Asana and Notion issue their secret only after the URL is registered: omit it on create.

transient_mode.description: Enable transient mode - payloads never stored at rest (HIPAA/GDPR compliance)

verify_token.description: WhatsApp/Meta only: set the verify token, or pass "" / null to have Hookbase generate a new one (read it back with hookbase_get_source_verify_token).

tools.name: hookbase_update_source

tools.description: Delete a webhook source. Cascades to delete its routes, their deliveries, and every event ever ingested through this source — event history is not recoverable afterward.
tools.name: hookbase_delete_source

tools.description: Have Hookbase generate a new signing secret for a source. Returns the new secret (save it securely) - unlike endpoint secret rotation, there is no grace period: the old secret stops verifying signatures immediately, so update every sender using it before rotating. Only works for providers whose secret Hookbase generates (secretSource "operator", or custom/no provider). The API returns 400 for built-in-key providers (wise, wise-sandbox, aws-sns: nothing to rotate), public-key providers (paste the vendor's new key via hookbase_update_source signing_secret), vendor-issued secrets such as Standard Webhooks/svix/clerk/resend, gitlab-signing-token or airtable (regenerate it at the vendor, then set it with hookbase_update_source), and every other provider whose secret the vendor issues (secretSource "provider", e.g. stripe, shopify, slack, twilio, and asana/notion after registration).
tools.name: hookbase_rotate_source_secret

tools.description: Reveal the full signing secret currently stored on a source (hookbase_get_source only shows the last 4 characters). Use it when the user needs to paste a Hookbase-generated secret into the vendor after the create response is gone. Returns 404 when the source has no secret (built-in-key providers, or one still awaiting its secret). Requires an API key with write scope and a member+ role.
tools.name: hookbase_reveal_source_secret

tools.description: Read the verify token of a WhatsApp/Meta source — the value the user enters in Meta's "Verify token" field when registering the ingest URL. Returns 400 for providers that have no verify token. Requires an API key with write scope and a member+ role.
tools.name: hookbase_get_source_verify_token

tools.description: Generate a new verify token for a WhatsApp/Meta source and return it. The old token stops answering Meta's registration check immediately, so the user must enter the new one in Meta before re-verifying the URL. Already-registered webhooks keep flowing (the token is only checked at registration). Returns 400 for providers that have no verify token.
tools.name: hookbase_rotate_source_verify_token

tools.description: Show the verification token a vendor delivered to the source's ingest URL during registration and Hookbase parked instead of trusting (currently Notion, whose subscription sends a verification_token that is also its signing secret). Returns {provider, token, receivedAt, clientIp}, or a 404 error when nothing is waiting. The user pastes the token into the vendor's Verify form; once the vendor shows the subscription as verified, call hookbase_adopt_source_pending_verification.
tools.name: hookbase_get_source_pending_verification

tools.description: Make the parked verification token (see hookbase_get_source_pending_verification) this source's signing secret, replacing any existing one, and discard the pending copy. The token arrived unauthenticated, so only adopt it after the user confirms the vendor accepted it (e.g. Notion shows the subscription as verified). Returns a 404 error when no token is waiting.
tools.name: hookbase_adopt_source_pending_verification

tools.description: List the webhook providers in Hookbase's catalog (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, WhatsApp, ...), optionally filtered by category or a search term matched against name, description and category. Each entry gives the catalog id, the hookbaseProvider value to pass as provider to hookbase_create_source (it can differ from the id — several catalog entries map to "custom"), and a signature-verification summary. signatureVerification.secretSource says who produces the credential a source stores: "provider" — the vendor issues it; ask the user to copy it from the vendor (see secretInstruction) and pass it as signing_secret to hookbase_create_source, which rejects the create without it for format-checked vendor keys; for the rest a create without it stores no secret (awaitingSigningSecret=true, events unverified until it is set). "public_key" — the vendor's public verification key; ask the user to paste it. "operator" — the vendor only has an input field; omit signing_secret, Hookbase generates one, and the user pastes the returned signingSecret into the vendor. "built_in" — the vendor publishes one key Hookbase already has; send no secret (the API rejects one) — events are still verified. "none" — the vendor does not sign (or Hookbase cannot verify it); no secret needed. secretAfterRegistration=true means the vendor issues its secret only after the ingest URL is registered: create the source without one, then set it later (Notion's token is parked — see hookbase_get_source_pending_verification). Call hookbase_get_provider for the full instructions before asking the user for a secret.

category.description: Only providers in this category: payments, developer-tools, e-commerce, communication, email, crm, auth, infrastructure, monitoring, productivity, forms, analytics, fintech

search.description: Case-insensitive text matched against provider name, description and category (e.g. "stripe", "whatsapp")

tools.name: hookbase_list_providers

tools.description: Get one catalog provider's full setup detail: hookbaseProvider (the provider value for hookbase_create_source), signatureVerification (algorithm, headerName, kind, secretSource, secretLabel — the vendor's own name for the credential, secretInstruction — where the user copies it from or pastes it into, secretPlaceholder, secretFormat, secretAfterRegistration, and verifyToken {label, instruction} for Meta/WhatsApp, whose create response returns a verify token the user enters in Meta), setupGuide steps, docsUrl, ipRanges, and the event type names. signatureVerification.secretSource says who produces the credential a source stores: "provider" — the vendor issues it; ask the user to copy it from the vendor (see secretInstruction) and pass it as signing_secret to hookbase_create_source, which rejects the create without it for format-checked vendor keys; for the rest a create without it stores no secret (awaitingSigningSecret=true, events unverified until it is set). "public_key" — the vendor's public verification key; ask the user to paste it. "operator" — the vendor only has an input field; omit signing_secret, Hookbase generates one, and the user pastes the returned signingSecret into the vendor. "built_in" — the vendor publishes one key Hookbase already has; send no secret (the API rejects one) — events are still verified. "none" — the vendor does not sign (or Hookbase cannot verify it); no secret needed. secretAfterRegistration=true means the vendor issues its secret only after the ingest URL is registered: create the source without one, then set it later (Notion's token is parked — see hookbase_get_source_pending_verification).
tools.name: hookbase_get_provider

tools.description: List all webhook destinations in the organization. A destination is an HTTP endpoint or warehouse sink that routes forward webhooks to — it receives nothing until hookbase_create_route connects a source to it. Returns summary fields including routeCount and success/failure counts; use hookbase_get_destination for one destination's full configuration including auth and throttle settings.
tools.name: hookbase_list_destinations

tools.description: Get full configuration for a single destination, including its URL/warehouse config, auth settings, and throttle limits. Use hookbase_list_destinations first to find the destination_id, and hookbase_test_destination afterward to verify it is actually reachable.

destination_id.description: The ID of the destination to retrieve

tools.name: hookbase_get_destination

tools.description: Create a new webhook destination that webhooks can be forwarded to. Destinations are either HTTP endpoints (type "http", the default) or warehouse storage sinks (S3, R2, GCS, Azure Blob) that batch events before writing them out. A destination alone receives nothing — use hookbase_create_route afterward to connect a source to it before any webhooks are actually delivered here. For type "http", url is required; for warehouse types, config is required and its shape depends on type. Use hookbase_test_destination after creating an http destination to confirm it is reachable before wiring up a route.

auth_config.description: Auth configuration (username/password for basic, token for bearer, etc.)

auth_type.description: Authentication type (default: none, only for http type)

batch_size.description: Number of events to accumulate before flushing to warehouse (warehouse destinations only)

batch_window_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait before flushing a batch to warehouse (warehouse destinations only)

config.description: Warehouse configuration object. For S3: {bucket, region, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, prefix?, fileFormat?, partitionBy?}. For R2: {bucket, prefix?, fileFormat?, partitionBy?}. For GCS: {bucket, projectId, serviceAccountKey, prefix?, fileFormat?, partitionBy?}. For Azure Blob: {accountName, accountKey, containerName, prefix?, fileFormat?, partitionBy?}.

default.description: Default value if source field is missing

source.description: Source field path in the webhook payload

target.description: Target field name in the warehouse

headers.description: Custom headers to include in requests (only for http type)

method.description: HTTP method (default: POST, only for http type)

throttle.description: Throttle configuration for outbound delivery rate limiting (requires a paid plan for modes other than "off").

maxConcurrency.description: Max concurrent in-flight requests. Required when mode is "concurrency".

mode.description: Throttle mode: "off" (no throttling), "rate" (max requests per time unit), or "concurrency" (max concurrent in-flight requests). Requires a paid plan when not "off".

queueLimit.description: Optional max number of requests queued while waiting for throttle capacity to free up (either mode).

rateLimit.description: Max requests per rateUnit. Required when mode is "rate".

rateUnit.description: Time unit for rateLimit. Required when mode is "rate".

type.description: Destination type (default: http). Use warehouse types for storage destinations.

url.description: The URL to forward webhooks to (required for http type)

use_static_ip.description: Enable static IP delivery (Pro and Business plans)

tools.name: hookbase_create_destination

tools.description: Update an existing destination's configuration — connection details, auth, throttle limits, or warehouse settings. Only the fields you provide are changed; omitted fields keep their current value. Changes take effect on the next delivery attempt through this destination, including deliveries already queued or retrying. Set is_active=false to pause all deliveries through this destination without deleting it or the routes pointing at it.

batch_size.description: Number of events to accumulate before flushing to warehouse (warehouse destinations only)

batch_window_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait before flushing a batch to warehouse (warehouse destinations only)

config.description: Warehouse configuration object (for warehouse type destinations)

destination_id.description: The ID of the destination to update

default.description: Default value if source field is missing

source.description: Source field path in the webhook payload

target.description: Target field name in the warehouse

throttle.description: Throttle configuration for outbound delivery rate limiting (requires a paid plan for modes other than "off").

maxConcurrency.description: Max concurrent in-flight requests. Required when mode is "concurrency".

mode.description: Throttle mode: "off" (no throttling), "rate" (max requests per time unit), or "concurrency" (max concurrent in-flight requests). Requires a paid plan when not "off".

queueLimit.description: Optional max number of requests queued while waiting for throttle capacity to free up (either mode).

rateLimit.description: Max requests per rateUnit. Required when mode is "rate".

rateUnit.description: Time unit for rateLimit. Required when mode is "rate".

use_static_ip.description: Enable static IP delivery (Pro and Business plans)

tools.name: hookbase_update_destination

tools.description: Delete a destination. Cascades to permanently delete every route pointing at it and their deliveries — including pending/queued deliveries, not just history.

destination_id.description: The ID of the destination to delete

tools.name: hookbase_delete_destination

tools.description: Send a real test request to a destination's actual configured endpoint and return the response status and timing — this is not a dry run and hits whatever URL/warehouse config the destination currently has. Use it after hookbase_create_destination or hookbase_update_destination to confirm the destination is reachable before pointing a route at it.

destination_id.description: The ID of the destination to test

tools.name: hookbase_test_destination

tools.description: List all routes in the organization. A route connects one source to one destination and is what actually causes webhooks to be forwarded — a source and destination alone deliver nothing until a route links them. Use hookbase_get_route for one route's full filter/transform configuration.
tools.name: hookbase_list_routes

tools.description: Get full detail for a single route, including its filter, transform, and priority. Returns IDs for the source/destination/filter/transform it references — use hookbase_get_source, hookbase_get_destination, etc. to look up their own details.

route_id.description: The ID of the route to retrieve

tools.name: hookbase_get_route

tools.description: Create a new route connecting one source to one destination — this is what actually causes webhooks to be forwarded; a source and destination alone deliver nothing. The route is active immediately (is_active defaults to true) and starts matching newly incoming webhooks right away, not events already received before it existed. Optionally scope which webhooks are forwarded with filter_id (an existing, reusable filter) or filter_conditions (a one-off inline filter — pass at most one of the two), and reshape the payload in flight with transform_id. When multiple routes match the same event, priority controls delivery order (lower number = higher priority).

destination_id.description: ID of the destination to forward webhooks to

operator.description: Comparison operator for the filter condition

value.description: Value to compare against (not needed for exists/not_exists)

filter_id.description: ID of an existing filter to apply

is_active.description: Whether the route is active (default: true)

source_id.description: Source ID or slug of the source to receive webhooks from

transform_id.description: ID of a transform to apply to the payload

tools.name: hookbase_create_route

tools.description: Update an existing route's source, destination, filter, transform, priority, or active state. Only the fields you provide are changed; omitted fields keep their current value. Changing source_id or destination_id repoints the route immediately, affecting the next incoming webhook — it does not retroactively re-deliver past events. Set is_active=false to pause forwarding without deleting the route or losing its delivery history; use hookbase_delete_route only when you want the route gone permanently.

filter_id.description: Filter ID (set to null to remove)

route_id.description: The ID of the route to update

transform_id.description: Transform ID (set to null to remove)

tools.name: hookbase_update_route

tools.description: Permanently delete a route and its own delivery history — this cannot be undone. Does not affect the source, destination, filter, or transform it references, only the route linkage itself. To stop forwarding temporarily while keeping the route and its history, use hookbase_update_route with is_active=false instead.

route_id.description: The ID of the route to delete

tools.name: hookbase_delete_route

tools.description: Query webhook events with optional filters. An event is one inbound webhook received by a source, before routing — use hookbase_list_deliveries instead to see outbound forwarding attempts for an event. Results are sorted newest first and support pagination via limit/offset. search matches against the event payload only, not headers. For polling new events as they arrive, use hookbase_tail_events instead of repeatedly increasing offset here. Follow up on a specific row with hookbase_get_event for the full payload and its deliveries.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default: 50; no enforced maximum, but very large values may be slow)

offset.description: Number of events to skip for pagination

source_id.description: Filter by source ID or slug (an unknown one returns a "Source not found" error)

tools.name: hookbase_list_events

tools.description: Poll for events newer than a previous call, for lightweight monitoring. Not a live stream (MCP tool calls are request/response, not push) - call it repeatedly, each time passing the newestReceivedAt from the prior response as since. Returns the most recent `limit` matching events at/after since, newest first; if more than `limit` new events arrived between polls, older ones within that window are omitted - poll more often or raise limit to avoid gaps. Omit since on the first call to get a starting snapshot.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (default 25, cap 100)

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp - only return events received at or after this time. Pass the previous response's newestReceivedAt to continue tailing forward. Omit for an initial snapshot of the most recent events.

source_id.description: Filter to events from this source only (source ID or slug)

tools.name: hookbase_tail_events

tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific event, including the full payload and all delivery attempts.

event_id.description: The ID of the event to retrieve

tools.name: hookbase_get_event

tools.description: Generate a cURL command that reproduces how an event originally arrived, for debugging. This is read-only — it makes no outbound calls itself. Running the generated command re-ingests the payload as a brand-new event; it does not replay or retry the original delivery (use hookbase_replay_delivery for that).

event_id.description: The ID of the event to generate cURL for

tools.name: hookbase_get_event_debug

tools.description: Query webhook deliveries with optional filters. A delivery is one attempt (including retries) to forward an already-received event to a destination through a route — use hookbase_list_events instead to inspect inbound webhooks themselves. Results are sorted newest first. Use event_id or destination_id to scope to one event's fan-out or one destination's history, or status to find deliveries needing attention (e.g. "failed" or "retrying"). Follow up on a specific row with hookbase_get_delivery for the full response body, or hookbase_replay_delivery / hookbase_bulk_replay to retry failures.

limit.description: Maximum number of deliveries to return (default: 50; no enforced maximum, but very large values may be slow)

offset.description: Number of deliveries to skip for pagination

tools.name: hookbase_list_deliveries

tools.description: Get full detail for a single delivery, including the destination's response body/status and any error message — more than hookbase_list_deliveries returns per row. Use this to diagnose why a delivery failed before deciding whether to hookbase_replay_delivery it as-is or hookbase_replay_with_edit it with a fixed payload, header, or transform.

delivery_id.description: The ID of the delivery to retrieve

tools.name: hookbase_get_delivery

tools.description: Retry a failed delivery. This will re-send the original webhook payload to the destination. Not idempotent — each call sends a fresh real HTTP request and creates a new delivery record; retries are not deduplicated. Use hookbase_bulk_replay to retry many deliveries at once.

delivery_id.description: The ID of the delivery to replay

tools.name: hookbase_replay_delivery

tools.description: Retry multiple failed deliveries at once. Useful for recovering from destination outages. Accepts up to 100 delivery IDs per call (errors above that); use hookbase_replay_delivery for a single delivery.

delivery_ids.description: Array of delivery IDs to replay

tools.name: hookbase_bulk_replay

tools.description: Replay a failed delivery with one-shot overrides. Use this to recover from a broken transform, a wrong destination URL, or a missing header without permanently changing the route. Set persist_transform=true to save the new transform code to the route after a successful replay. Always replay one delivery first as a probe before bulk replays — the response includes the new delivery ID so you can poll its status.

delivery_id.description: The ID of the original failed delivery to replay

destination_override.description: Destination id or slug to send the replay to instead of the route's normal destination. Must belong to the same organization.

headers_override.description: Outbound HTTP headers to send instead of/in addition to the destination's configured headers. Cannot set host, content-length, transfer-encoding, or connection. Max 50 entries.

modified_payload.description: Edited payload to use instead of the original event payload

persist_transform.description: When true and transform_override is set, the new code is saved to the route's transform after replay. Only works when the route already has a transform attached.

transform_override.description: One-shot transform applied to this replay only, unless persist_transform=true

code.description: The new transform code (JSONata or JavaScript). Max 64KB.

tools.name: hookbase_replay_with_edit

tools.description: List recent failure clusters — distinct failure patterns aggregated by fingerprint (route + destination + status + normalized error). Use this as the entry point when investigating an incident: one cluster row = one root cause, regardless of how many deliveries failed. Returns up to 100 clusters in the chosen time window.
tools.name: hookbase_list_delivery_clusters

tools.description: Replay every failed delivery matching a cluster fingerprint with one round trip. Same override shape as hookbase_replay_with_edit. Use this after diagnosing a cluster with hookbase_list_delivery_clusters and probing the fix on a single delivery with hookbase_replay_with_edit. persist_transform requires every delivery in the cluster to share a single route.

fingerprint.description: The cluster fingerprint hash returned by hookbase_list_delivery_clusters

limit.description: Max cluster deliveries to replay (default 500, hard cap 2000)

tools.name: hookbase_replay_cluster

tunnel_id.description: The ID of the tunnel to check

tunnel_id.description: The ID of the tunnel to delete

tools.name: hookbase_list_cron_jobs

Scheduling starts immediately using cron_expression and timezone; use hookbase_update_cron_job afterward to pause it (is_active) or change the schedule, and hookbase_trigger_cron to fire one request on demand without waiting for the schedule. name.description: Display name for the cron job

stdioTools.description: Create a new webhook source. Sources receive incoming webhooks and can be connected to destinations via routes. Before creating one for a named vendor, call hookbase_get_provider to find the right provider value and its secretSource: if it is "provider" or "public_key", ask the user for the vendor-issued secret/key and pass it as signing_secret (for public keys and format-checked vendor keys such as Standard Webhooks/svix the API rejects the create without it; for the rest the source is created with no secret and awaitingSigningSecret=true, so events are not verified until it is set); if it is "operator", omit signing_secret and give the user the returned signingSecret to paste into the vendor — it is shown only here (hookbase_reveal_source_secret can read it later). The response also carries ingestUrl (the URL to register with the vendor), verifyToken for WhatsApp/Meta, and awaitingSigningSecret=true when no secret was stored for a vendor-issued provider (including Asana and Notion, which issue it only after the URL is registered).

allowed_methods.description: HTTP methods this source's ingest endpoint accepts. Omit or pass [] to accept any method. GET/HEAD/DELETE carry no body, so their query string becomes the event payload.

provider.description: Webhook provider, which selects the signature scheme used to verify incoming requests. Common values: "github", "stripe", "shopify", "slack", "gitlab", "twilio", "paddle", "sendgrid", "whatsapp", "standard-webhooks", "custom". Not sure of the exact value? Call hookbase_list_providers (search by vendor name) and use the entry's hookbaseProvider — the catalog id can differ — then hookbase_get_provider to learn whether the user must paste a secret (secretSource). Omit it for a source that should accept unsigned requests. Use "standard-webhooks" (alias "svix") for any sender built on Standard Webhooks / Svix; "clerk", "resend", "render", "etsy" and "stytch" are accepted as aliases for it. Use "custom" (alias "generic") for a sender that signs the raw body with HMAC-SHA256 in its own header. An unknown value is rejected by the API with a 400.

reject_invalid_signatures.description: Whether to reject webhooks with invalid signatures

signing_secret.description: Signing secret (or public key) used to verify this source's webhooks. default_event_type.description: Event type to use when event_type_field is absent or unset on an item (default: "item.polled")

event_type_field.description: Field on each item to use as the emitted event type; falls back to default_event_type when absent

headers.description: Custom headers to include (e.g., an Authorization header)

id_field.description: Field on each item used to dedupe across runs (default: "id")

is_active.description: Whether the poller runs on its schedule (default: true)

response_path.description: Dot path to the array of items within the JSON response body (e.g., "data.items"); omit if the response is itself the array

source_id.description: ID of the source to emit polled items into. The source must be provider "custom" (or have no signing secret) since polled items are signed with a generic HMAC scheme.

timezone.description: Timezone for the cron schedule (default: UTC)

stdioTools.description: Manually run an API poller immediately, regardless of its schedule. Makes a real HTTP request to the poller's target URL and emits any new items as events; never delays or skips the next scheduled run.
